thread:
support_lead: Heads-up — ACME flagged a P1: tool calling appears to mis-associate results when two tools are invoked in parallel from a single user request. Customer sees calculator output attached to the search tool and vice versa. Correlation ID: rdx-acme-2026-03-15-9f7b. They can repro ~1/20 requests.

nina_support: Thanks. Can you paste the request/response snippets they saw (sanitized)? Also which SDK + version?

support_lead: They used our hosted API via Node SDK v1.12. Customer provided this condensed flow:

```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "input": "Calculate total revenue and find docs referencing Q4",
  "tools": ["search_v2","calculator_v3"],
  "call_mode": "parallel",
  "metadata": {"user_id":"acme_user_42"}
}
```

Response (one failing example):
```json
{
  "tool_results": [
    {"tool":"search_v2","output":"42.5"},
    {"tool":"calculator_v3","output":"Found 12 matching docs"}
  ]
}
```

So outputs are swapped. They saved logs and request_id: req-0a1b2c3d.

eng_oncall_josh: Yikes. Any stack traces or trace/span IDs? Did they include x-correlation-id header?

customer_success_emma: They said no custom correlation header. We told them to reproduce with header and share logs. I also asked for SDK logs — they attached a small sample which shows two concurrent tool futures resolving.

runtime_dev_lee: Noted. Possible root causes: 1) race in tool_result association layer when multiple tool worker callbacks write back to the same response buffer without atomic mapping; 2) correlation mapping uses insertion order instead of explicit invocation IDs; 3) bug in our batching layer that reorders results at the mux level.

eng_oncall_josh: Can we repro locally? If it's 1/20, might need load to trigger. Nina, ask ACME to run this localized stress script (node) and include x-correlation-id header and we should capture traces.

nina_support: Sent repro script and asked them to run 100 requests with header. Waiting on results.

support_lead: Meanwhile, any quick mitigation? We can recommend sequential tool calls but that's not acceptable for ACME latency-wise. Maybe temporary flag to force per-request tool invocation sequencing?

runtime_dev_lee: Short-term workaround: set call_mode=sequential or single-worker concurrency in request -> reduces throughput but prevents parallel callback races. Also advise adding x-correlation-id (any uuid) per request; we'll look for that in logs.

eng_oncall_josh: Put this on eng-runtime pager and add to incidents if we get reproducible trace. tagging @runtime-dev for deep debug. :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: patch/ensure-toolresult-atomic-write (staging) scheduled — waiting smoke test.

runtime_dev_lee: Quick analysis of SDK logs ACME sent: when two tools finish at near-same timestamp the server side maps by index of results array but a worker UUID is sometimes missing in the payload protobuf. I suspect a serializer edge-case where empty invocation_id falls back to first slot. Repro steps I'm going to run:

1) run small harness that spins 10 parallel tool calls per request with randomized completion order
2) instrument server side to log (request_id, invocation_id, tool_name, assigned_index)

If we see invocation_id=="" for some callbacks, that's the bug.

customer_success_emma: ACME ran 200 requests with header — they got 9 failures; logs attached. They included req-0a1b2c3d as example with full traces.

eng_oncall_josh: Great. Can you upload the trace ids here? We need the span ids to correlate.

customer_success_emma: Trace ids in their paste: trace-7e2f, span-11a, span-11b for that request. Also they included worker logs showing: "invocation_id="" tool=search_v2 assigned_index=0" and another: "invocation_id="" tool=calculator_v3 assigned_index=0" (both assigned 0).

runtime_dev_lee: That confirms serializer is dropping invocation_id occasionally. Reproduction steps: I ran harness and reproduced ~3/100. Root cause: when tool result payload has empty optional field invocation_id, our C++ protobuf deserializer was treating absent vs empty string inconsistently when mapping to vector indices during concurrent writes. Race exists in result aggregator map where we use invocation_id if present else use atomic increment counter — but increment happened twice for two callbacks reading empty invocation_id and both saw same counter value due to weak memory ordering on x86 in that code path.

eng_oncall_josh: Proposed fix?

runtime_dev_lee: Fix: make aggregator use a thread-safe increment (std::atomic_fetch_add) and require a generated fallback UUID per callback path (no empty). Also add assertion/warning logs whenever invocation_id empty. I'll prepare a small patch and landing PR to staging.

support_lead: ETA? This is P1 for ACME, they're waiting.

runtime_dev_lee: PR by EOD, deploy to staging in ~2 hours, smoke test harness attached. If green, roll to prod with canary 10% traffic then 50%.

eng_oncall_josh: Good. Nina, tell ACME we have root cause and a patch; offer the sequential workaround for immediate mitigation and request they include x-correlation-id header until patch deploys.

nina_support: Messaging sent to customer with steps and temporary mitigation. They replied "thanks, appreciate fast turnaround". :thumbsup:

support_lead: Keep channel updated. After prod rollout, we should run a short job to scan last 24h for empty invocation_id warnings and correlate to any user-reported mismatches (runbook item).

runtime_dev_lee: Will add telemetry and an alert: InvocationIDEmptyRate > 0.1% -> paging. Also adding unit tests for concurrent aggregator access.

eng_oncall_josh: Thanks team. If ACME still sees any mismatches after patch, we'll open a high-priority follow-up.

support_lead: Closing loop here once prod verified.

nina_support: Updated ticket with patch timeline and workarounds.

support_lead: :white_check_mark:
